data: There is plenty of room at the bottom” is a succinct expression by Feynman about the richness of the quantum world. How do we harness this abundance? In this course, we attempt to answer this question. Peter Shor designing a quantum search algorithm that is much faster than any known classical algorithm marked the beginning of a new paradigm. The most relevant aspect is the way we process information. Doing it the quantum way speeds up the process, makes it more efficient and surpasses, in many cases, the limits known from a classical perspective. This course begins with a discussion on information theory and introduces ideas about quantum information processing (QIP). Other topics to be covered include quantum algorithms and their experimental implementations. Students will learn to program the IBM quantum computer as well. Major corporates in IT and many leading institutes have strong research programs in QIP. That vouches for the importance of this science.
